actions.name: NodeAcceleration
actions.desc: Controls the movement of the node. This is the most basic action for controlling the acceleration of nodes.

speedZ.desc: Controls the speed of the node along its Z-axis.

accelerationZ.desc: Controls the acceleration of the node along its Z-axis. This value cannot be negative.

accelerationY.desc: Controls the acceleration of the node along its Y-axis.

unk_ds3_f1_1.desc: This is replaces {@link unkAlignWithMotion} in DS3 and Sekiro only. When set to 1, this seems to just stop the positional motion from this action entirely.

unkAlignWithMotion.desc: When set to 1, this makes the node align with the direction it's moving. Setting it to higher values seems to do the same as setting it to 0, which means it's probably not a boolean, but what those values do exactly is unknown.

actions.name: Unk11
actions.desc: Unknown.

actions.name: NodeTranslation
actions.desc: Translates the node using a property, meaning it can be animated. This can be useful if you need the node to follow a specific path.

translation.desc: An offset for the position of the node.

unkAlignWithMotion.desc: When set to 1, this makes the node align with the direction it's moving. There are cases of this being set to 2 in vanilla, and it seems to behave similarly to when it is set to 0, so this is not a boolean. The actual differences between 0 and 2 are unknown.

actions.name: NodeSpin

angularSpeedZ.desc: The node's angular speed around its local Z-axis in degrees per second.

actions.name: StaticNodeTransform
actions.desc: Controls the translation and rotation of a node.

offset.desc:
Translation of the node.

This translation happens after all {@link rotation rotations}, meaning the rotations will not affect the translation.

rotation.desc:
The rotation of the node.

The order the rotations happen in is Z -> X -> Y, and the translation from {@link offset} happens after all rotations.

actions.name: RandomNodeTransform
actions.desc: Controls the translation and rotation of a node, and can also randomize them.

offset.desc:
Translation of the node.

This translation happens after all {@link rotation rotations}, meaning the rotations will not affect the translation.

rotation.desc:
The rotation of the node.

The order the rotations happen in is Z -> X -> Y, and the translation from {@link offset} happens after all rotations.

offsetVariance.desc: The maximum random change in translation of the node. A random value between the {@link offset base value} minus this and the base value plus this will be the final offset used.

rotationVariance.desc: The maximum random change in rotation of the node. A random value between the {@link rotation base value} minus this and the base value plus this will be the final rotation used.

actions.name: NodeAttachToCamera

followRotation.desc: Disable this to stop the node from following the rotation of the camera.

actions.name: ParticleAcceleration
actions.desc: Controls the movement of particles. This is the most basic action for controlling the acceleration of particles.

gravity.desc:
Controls the acceleration of the particle along the global Y-axis. Positive values will make the particles go down, and negative values will go up.

Unless it's left at 0, this changes the current direction of the particles, which can affect various other things, for example the rotation of {@link ActionType.Line Line} and {@link ActionType.QuadLine QuadLine} particles, and the direction of this action's {@link acceleration}. It does not affect the particles' {@link InitialDirection initial direction}.

acceleration.desc: The particles' acceleration in their current direction, which is usually their {@link InitialDirection initial direction}, but can be changed over time by other things, for example this action's {@link gravity}.

actions.name: NodeAttributes
actions.desc: Controls various things about the node, like its duration, and how it is attached to the parent node.

duration.desc: The node duration in seconds. Can be set to -1 to make the node last forever.

delay.desc: The delay in seconds before the node becomes active.

attachment.desc: Controls how the node is attached to the parent node.

depthBias.desc:
Controls the rendering order of this node. Lower values will cause the node to be drawn in front of nodes with a higher value. This only affects the node with this action, it is not inherited by descendant nodes.

This does not affect the actual depth of the node in the scene. It will still draw behind other objects even with a big negative bias. It only affects the order it is rendered in relative to other effects.

Model particles and light sources are not affected by this in any way. Most, if not all, other types of appearances are affected by it, even GPU particles and lens flares.

actions.name: ParticleAttributes
actions.desc: Controls the duration of particles emitted by the node, and how the particles are attached to the node.

duration.desc: The particle duration in seconds. Can be set to -1 to make particles last forever.

attachment.desc: Controls how the particles are attached to the node.

actions.name: Unk130
actions.desc: Unknown action that is in every basic config in every game, and still literally nothing is known about it.

actions.name: ParticleModifier
actions.desc:
Modifies particles in various ways.

Note: This is **not** a {@link Modifier property modifier}, it is an action that modifies particles emitted from the same node.

speed.desc: Controls the speed of the particles emitted from this node, but only if the config has an action in the {@link ActionSlots.ParticleMovementAction ParticleMovement slot} that enables acceleration of particles. The direction is the particle's {@link InitialDirection initial direction}.

scaleX.desc:
Multiplier for the scale along the X-axis for the particles emitted from this node.

If {@link uniformScale} is enabled, this also affects the Y and Z axes.

scaleY.desc:
Multiplier for the scale along the Y-axis for the particles emitted from this node.

If {@link uniformScale} is enabled, {@link scaleX} also affects the Y-axis, and this property is ignored.

scaleZ.desc:
Multiplier for the scale along the Z-axis for the particles emitted from this node.

If {@link uniformScale} is enabled, {@link scaleX} also affects the Z-axis, and this property is ignored.

color.desc:
Color multiplier for the particles emitted from this node.

Values in this are unrestricted and can go above 1.

uniformScale.desc: Scales the particles emitted from this node uniformly based on {@link scaleX}. The other scale properties in this action have no effect when this is enabled.

actions.name: SFXReference
actions.desc: References another SFX by its ID.

sfx.desc: The ID of the referenced SFX.

actions.name: LevelsOfDetailThresholds
actions.desc: Used in the {@link ConfigType.LevelsOfDetail levels of detail config} to manage the duration and thresholds for the {@link NodeType.LevelsOfDetail levels of detail node}.

duration.desc: The node duration in seconds. Can be set to -1 to make the node last forever.

actions.name: StateConfigMap
actions.desc: Maps states to configs in the parent node.

configIndices.desc:
A list of config indices.

The index of each value represents the index of the state, and the value represents the index of the config that should be active when the state is active.

actions.name: SelectAllNodes
actions.desc: Used in {@link ConfigType.NodeEmitter NodeEmitter configs} to emit all child nodes every emission.

actions.name: SelectRandomNode
actions.desc: Used in {@link ConfigType.NodeEmitter NodeEmitter configs} to emit a random child node every emission.

weights.desc:
Probability weights for each child node to be selected for emission.

The weights are stored as integers, so non-integer values in this list will be truncated.

actions.name: PeriodicEmitter
actions.desc: Emits particles periodically.

interval.desc: Time between emitting new particles in seconds.

perEmission.desc: The number of particles or nodes to emit per emission.

totalEmissions.desc:
The total number of emissions. Once this limit is reached, the branch will be *removed from the effect*. The node and all of its descendants will be destroyed, and there are no ways to re-enable them without respawning the entire effect as they no longer exist.

Can be set to `-1` to disable the limit.

maxConcurrent.desc: Maximum number of concurrent emitted particles or nodes. Can be set to `-1` to disable the limit.

actions.name: EqualDistanceEmitter
actions.desc: Emits particles once it has moved a certain distance from where it last emitted particles.

threshold.desc: How much the emitter must move to trigger emission.

totalEmissions.desc:
The total number of emissions. Once this limit is reached, the branch will be *removed from the effect*. The node and all of its descendants will be destroyed, and there are no ways to re-enable them without respawning the entire effect as they no longer exist.

Can be set to `-1` to disable the limit.

maxConcurrent.desc: Maximum number of concurrent emitted particles or nodes. Can be set to `-1` to disable the limit.

actions.name: OneTimeEmitter
actions.desc: Emits one particle once.

actions.name: PointEmitterShape
actions.desc: Makes the emitter a single point.

direction.desc: Controls the initial direction for particles. See {@link InitialDirection} for more information.

actions.name: DiskEmitterShape
actions.desc: Makes the emitter disk-shaped.

distribution.desc:
Controls how the random emission points are distributed within the disk.
- At 0, particles are equally likely to emit from anywhere inside the disk.
- At 1, particles have a 100% chance of being emitted from the center point.
- At -1, particles have a 100% chance of being emitted from the perimeter circle of the disk.
- Values between these smoothly blend between them.

direction.desc: Controls the initial direction for particles. See {@link InitialDirection} for more information.

actions.name: RectangleEmitterShape
actions.desc: Makes the emitter rectangular.

distribution.desc:
Controls how the random emission points are distributed within the rectangle.
- At 0, particles are equally likely to emit from anywhere inside the rectangle.
- At 1, particles have a 100% chance of being emitted from the center point.
- At -1, particles have a 100% chance of being emitted from the perimeter of the rectangle.
- Values between these smoothly blend between them.

direction.desc: Controls the initial direction for particles. See {@link InitialDirection} for more information.

actions.name: SphereEmitterShape
actions.desc: Makes the emitter spherical.

emitInside.desc: If true, particles will be emitted from anywhere within the sphere. Otherwise the particles will be emitted only from the surface of the sphere.

actions.name: BoxEmitterShape
actions.desc: Makes the emitter cuboidal.

direction.desc: Controls the initial direction for particles. See {@link InitialDirection} for more information.

emitInside.desc: If true, particles will be emitted from anywhere within the cuboid. Otherwise the particles will be emitted only from the surface of the cuboid.

actions.name: CylinderEmitterShape
actions.desc: Makes the emitter cylindrical.

direction.desc: Controls the initial direction for particles. See {@link InitialDirection} for more information.

emitInside.desc: If true, particles will be emitted from anywhere within the cylinder. Otherwise the particles will be emitted only from the surface of the cylinder, excluding the ends.

yAxis.desc: If true, the cylinder will be aligned with the Y-axis instead of the Z-axis.

actions.name: NoSpread
actions.desc: Makes all emitted instances have the default initial direction from the emitter. See {@link InitialDirection} for more information.

actions.name: CircularSpread
actions.desc: Gives each emitted instance a random initial direction offset within a circular cone. See {@link InitialDirection} for more information.

angle.desc: The maximum change in direction in degrees, the angle of the cone.

distribution.desc:
Controls the distribution of the random directions that can be chosen.
- At 0, all directions within the cone have an equal chance of being chosen.
- At 1, the default direction is guaranteed to be chosen.
- At -1, the maximum change in direction is guaranteed, meaning the chosen direction will always be a fixed number of degrees away from the default direction based on {@link angle}.
- Values between these values smoothly blend between them.
- Values outside of the -1 to 1 range also work, but may do some unexpected things.

unk_er_f1_0.desc: No so much unknown, just unnamed. If enabled, this limits the possible directions to only positive values on one axis, effectively cutting the cone of possible directions in half.

actions.name: EllipticalSpread
actions.desc: Gives each emitted instance a random initial direction offset within an elliptical cone. See {@link InitialDirection} for more information.

angleX.desc: The maximum change in direction in degrees, one of the angles of the elliptical cone.

angleY.desc: The maximum change in direction in degrees, one of the angles of the elliptical cone.

distribution.desc:
Controls the distribution of the random directions that can be chosen.
- At 0, all directions within the cone have an equal chance of being chosen.
- At 1, the default direction is guaranteed to be chosen.
- At -1, the maximum change in direction is guaranteed, meaning the chosen direction will always be a fixed number of degrees away from the default direction based on {@link angleX} and {@link angleY}.
- Values between these values smoothly blend between them.
- Values outside of the -1 to 1 range also work, but may do some unexpected things.

unk_er_f1_0.desc: No so much unknown, just unnamed. If enabled, this limits the possible directions to only positive values on one axis, effectively cutting the cone of possible directions in half.

actions.name: RectangularSpread
actions.desc: Gives each emitted instance a random initial direction offset within a rectangular cone. See {@link InitialDirection} for more information.

angleX.desc: The maximum change in direction in degrees, one of the angles of the elliptical cone.

angleY.desc: The maximum change in direction in degrees, one of the angles of the elliptical cone.

distribution.desc:
Controls the distribution of the random directions that can be chosen.
- At 0, all directions within the cone have an equal chance of being chosen.
- At 1, the default direction is guaranteed to be chosen.
- At -1, the maximum change in direction is guaranteed, meaning the chosen direction will always be a fixed number of degrees away from the default direction based on {@link angleX} and {@link angleY}.

actions.desc:
Defines a very basic point sprite particle. Similar to {@link BillboardEx}, but far simpler.

The name is from Elden Ring's RTTI, where it is named "GXFXCGAppearancePointSprite".

color1.desc:
Color multiplier.

Values in this will be clamped to the 0-1 range. To use values outside of this range, see {@link color3}.

Values greater than 100 will make the trail never reach full opacity. For example, a value of 200 will make the trail fade from 0 opacity at the start to 50% (100% / 200%) at the end of the trail.

If this value and {@link endFadeEndpoint} sum to a value greater than 100, the trail will be "split" at the point controlled by this value and each part will fade separately based on the repsective value. For example, if this is set to 50 and {@link endFadeEndpoint} is 1000, the first half of the trail will fade normally from 0 opacity at the start to full opacity at the mid point, but the other half will fade from 5% opacity ((100% - 50%) / 1000%) at the mid point to 0 at the end. actions.name: PointLight
actions.desc: Defines a point light source.

diffuseColor.desc:
Controls the diffuse color of the light.

Values in this are unrestricted and can go above 1.

If {@link separateSpecular} is disabled, this also controls the specular color of the light.

specularColor.desc:
Controls the specular color of the light.

Values in this are unrestricted and can go above 1.

If {@link separateSpecular} is disabled, this property is ignored and {@link diffuseColor} controls both the diffuse as well as the specular color.

radius.desc: The maximum distance that the light may travel from the source, and the radius of the sphere in which other effects caused by the light source (for example {@link volumeDensity} and its related fields) may act.

unk_ds3_p2_0.desc:
Affects the falloff of the light in some way, and how the normal of surfaces affect the intensity of the light.
- At 0 or negative values, this completely disables the light.
- At 1, the light behaves normally, like you would expect it to.
- At values between 0 and 1, it seemingly makes the falloff of the light over distance stronger, so the light will sooner fade to nothing.
- At values greater than 1, it will make the falloff weaker until near the {@link radius maximum distance}, and then it will very quickly fade to nothing. It also makes the normal of the surfaces hit by the light matter less. At very high values, anything within the radius basically becomes full bright.

diffuseMultiplier.desc:
A scalar multiplier for the {@link diffuseColor diffuse color}. Good for easily adjusting the brightness of the light without changing the color.

If {@link separateSpecular} is disabled, this also affects the specular color of the light.

specularMultiplier.desc:
A scalar multiplier for the {@link specularColor specular color}.

If {@link separateSpecular} is disabled, this property is ignored.

jitterAndFlicker.desc: Toggles the jitter and flicker animations for the light.

jitterAcceleration.desc: Controls the acceleration of the jittering.

jitterX.desc: Controls how much the light should move around randomly on the X-axis.

jitterY.desc: Controls how much the light should move around randomly on the Y-axis.

jitterZ.desc: Controls how much the light should move around randomly on the Z-axis.

flickerIntervalMin.desc: Controls the minimum interval for flickering.

flickerIntervalMax.desc: Controls the maximum interval for flickering.

flickerBrightness.desc: Brightness multiplier for the light when it flickers.

shadows.desc:
Controls if the light should have shadows or not.

Note: Map objects also have a setting for casting shadows, and both must be enabled for an object to cast shadows from the light source.

separateSpecular.desc: When enabled, this allows other properties and fields of the action to control the specular color independently of the diffuse color. When disabled, the diffuse counterpart of the properties or fields will affect both the diffuse and specular color.

fadeOutTime.desc:
The number of seconds the light takes to fade to nothing after being destroyed.

Due to how the field this represents works, the time will be rounded to the nearest multiple of 1/30s.

shadowDarkness.desc: Controls how dark shadows from this light source are. At 0, the shadows will be entirely invisible.

maxViewDistance.desc:
Controls the maximum distance for the light source to be active. If the camera is farther away from the light source than this distance, it will stop emitting light.

Setting this to `0` will disable the distance limit.

volumeDensity.desc: Controls the density of some sort of fake fog in the volume hit by the light. The fog does not affect the actual light produced by the source and is not affected by shadows.

phaseFunction.desc: Controls whether or not {@link asymmetryParam} affects the fake fog from {@link volumeDensity}.

asymmetryParam.desc:
Controls how the fake fog from {@link volumeDensity} scatters the light. This value is ignored if {@link phaseFunction} is disabled, and the fog will scatter the light equally in all directions.

- At 0, the light is scattered equally in every direction.
- As the value approaches 1, the light is scattered more and more forward, in the same direction as the light was already traveling. This means that the fake fog will be less visible from the side or behind, and more visible from in front of the light.
- At 1, the fog will not scatter the light at all, so it will be entirely invisible.
- Values above 1 produce unnatural-looking effects where the light darkens the fog instead.

adaptationExponent.desc: When not in a dark enough area, the brightness of the light will be multiplied by 0.1^α, where α is this exponent value. The light will have normal brightness when the area it's in is sufficiently dark.

actions.name: SimulateTermination

Note: An effect terminates when it reaches {@link State} -1.

actions.desc:
Allows the effect to continue playing normally after it terminates, but its opacity will gradually fade out over a given duration.

Note: An effect terminates when it reaches {@link State} -1.

actions.name: ParticleForceCollision
actions.desc:
Enables particles emitted by the node to collide with surfaces, and controls how those collisions affect the movement of the particles.

Note that this works very differently from the collision-related fields in the GPU particle appearance actions. The collision detection for those are entriely based on the distances between the camera and everything in its view, so if a particle is farther away from the camera than an object, the particle will be able to collide with it. The collision detection used in this action is based on the real 3D geometry of the scene, so particles can collide with anything, even while they are out of view.

Also note that this action seems to cause the game to crash very easily. If a particle affected by this action despawns due to its limited duration, the game will crash no matter what.

radius.desc: The collision radius of the particles. This controls the maximum distance between the particles and a surface they can collide with for a collision to be detected.

friction.desc:
The friction coefficient of the particles. This controls how quickly particles stop while sliding against a surface.
| Values | Behavior |
|-|-|
| <0 | The particles will accelerate as they slide, going faster and faster over time. |
| 0 | The particles will not decelerate at all as they slide. They will just keep sliding forever unless something else stops them. |
| 0-1 | The particles will decelerate as they slide, causing them to eventually come to a stop. |
| ≥1 | The particles will stop immediately if they contact a surface. They may still {@link bounciness bounce}, but they will never slide along the surface. |

bounciness.desc:
The coefficient of restitution of the particles, or how "bouncy" they are.
| Values | Behavior |
|-|-|
| ≤0 | Completely inelastic collision. The particles will not bounce if they hit something. They will just stop or slide.
| 0-1 | Partially elastic collision. The particles will bounce, but they will lose some energy from the collision, causing them to bounce back at a reduced speed compared to the speed they had before the collision. |
| 1 | Perfectly elastic collision. No energy is lost from any collision, causing the particles to bounce off at the same speed they hit the surface. |
| >1 | Hyper-elastic collision. The particles will gain energy from every collision, causing them to speed up every time they collide with something. Hitting something at an angle may in some cases still cause them to lose some energy. |

actions.name: Tracer
actions.desc:
Defines a tracer particle, which leaves a textured trail where it moves.

This is a newer version of {@link LegacyTracer} with more features, like being able to make the opacity of the trail be based on the movement speed of the particle.

The name is from Elden Ring's RTTI, where it is named "GXFfxAppearanceTracer".

startFadeEndpoint.desc:
Percentage along the trail from the start of the trail where the trail's opacity will start fading out towards the start. The trail will have 0 opacity at the start, and it will linearly increase towards full opacity at the point represented by this percentage.

The percentage is of the way from the start of the trail to the end of it, so if the trail gets longer or shorter, this point will move with it.

Values greater than 100 will make the trail never reach full opacity. For example, a value of 200 will make the trail fade from 0 opacity at the start to 50% (100% / 200%) at the end of the trail.

If this value and {@link endFadeEndpoint} sum to a value greater than 100, the trail will be "split" at the point controlled by this value and each part will fade separately based on the repsective value. For example, if this is set to 50 and {@link endFadeEndpoint} is 1000, the first half of the trail will fade normally from 0 opacity at the start to full opacity at the mid point, but the other half will fade from 5% opacity ((100% - 50%) / 1000%) at the mid point to 0 at the end. Where the two parts meet, the opacity will fade from one to the other across a single segment of the trail.

endFadeEndpoint.desc:
Percentage along the trail from the end of the trail where the trail's opacity will start fading out towards the end. The trail will have full opacity at the point represented by this percentage, and it will linearly decrease towards 0 opacity at the end.

The percentage is of the way from the end of the trail to the start of it, so if the trail gets longer or shorter, this point will move with it.

Values greater than 100 will make the trail never reach full opacity. For example, a value of 200 will make the trail fade from 0 opacity at the end to 50% (100% / 200%) at the start of the trail.

If this value and {@link startFadeEndpoint} sum to a value greater than 100, the trail will be "split" at the point controlled by {@link startFadeEndpoint} and each part will fade separately based on the repsective value. For example, if {@link startFadeEndpoint} is set to 50 and this is 1000, the first half of the trail will fade normally from 0 opacity at the start to full opacity at the mid point, but the other half will fade from 5% opacity ((100% - 50%) / 1000%) at the mid point to 0 at the end. Where the two parts meet, the opacity will fade from one to the other across a single segment of the trail.

color1.desc:
Color multiplier.

Values in this will be clamped to the 0-1 range. To use values outside of this range, see {@link color3}.

color2.desc:
Color multiplier.

Values in this will be clamped to the 0-1 range. There is no equivalent property with unrestricted values based on the emission time of the particle, but {@link color3} is still multiplicative with this and can be used to scale the values indirectly.

color3.desc:
Color multiplier.

Values in this are unrestricted and can go above 1. If you want values to be clamped to the 0-1 range, see {@link color1}.

alphaFadeThreshold.desc:
Parts of the particle with less opacity than this threshold will be invisible. The range is 0-255.

Values above this threshold will be stretched to fill the alpha range, so values near the threshold will be less visible, creating a smooth transition between the parts that have been hidden by the threshold and the ones that are still visible.

The index of the frame to show from the texture atlas. Can be animated using a {@link PropertyFunction.Linear linear property} or similar.

Seemingly identical to {@link frameIndexOffset}? The sum of these two properties is the actual frame index that gets used.

segmentInterval.desc: The trail is made up of multiple quads, or *segments*. This controls how many seconds to wait between new segments being created. Lower values produce a smoother trail.

segmentDuration.desc: The trail is made up of multiple quads, or *segments*. This controls how long each segment should last in seconds.

concurrentSegments.desc: The trail is made up of multiple quads, or *segments*. This controls how many segments may exist at the same time.

segmentSubdivision.desc:
The trail is made up of multiple quads, or *segments*. This controls how many times each completed segment should be subdivided. Higher values makes the trail look smoother.

A "completed" segment is any segment that is not the leading one. The leading segment has one side attached to the end of the previous segment and the other attached to the tracer source, and is always a simple quad.

fadeOutTime.desc: When the particle is meant to terminate, the trail will linger for this many seconds and its opacity will fade to 0 in that time.

totalFrames.desc: To split the texture into multiple animation frames, this value must be set to the total number of frames in the texture.

attachedUV.desc: Controls whether or not the UV of the trail should be attached to the node or not. If it is attached, the texture will slide along the segments to follow the source wherever it moves, as if it was a flag attached to a pole. If it is not attached, the texture will stay where it was when the segment was created, like a skid mark on a road where the road is the segments and the mark is the texture, it wouldn't follow the car/node that made it.

actions.name: RichModel
actions.desc:
Defines a particle with a 3D model. Similar to {@link Model}, but with some different options.

Some models only work properly with this action and not with the Model action for some unknown reason. A good example of this is the Carian greatsword model in Elden Ring (88300), which gets horribly stretched and distorted when used with the other action, but it works fine with this one.

The name is from Elden Ring's RTTI, where it is named "GXFfxAppearanceRichModel".

sizeX.desc:
The width of the particle.

If {@link uniformScale} is enabled, this also controls the height and depth.

sizeY.desc:
The height of the particle.

If {@link uniformScale} is enabled, {@link sizeX} also controls the height, and this property is ignored.

sizeZ.desc:
The depth of the particle.

If {@link uniformScale} is enabled, {@link sizeX} also controls the depth, and this property is ignored.

rotationX.desc: Rotation around the X-axis in degrees.

rotationY.desc: Rotation around the Y-axis in degrees.

rotationZ.desc: Rotation around the Z-axis in degrees.

angularSpeedX.desc: Angular speed around the X-axis in degrees per second.

angularSpeedY.desc: Angular speed around the Y-axis in degrees per second.

angularSpeedZ.desc: Angular speed around the Z-axis in degrees per second.

color1.desc:
Color multiplier.

Values in this will be clamped to the 0-1 range. To use values outside of this range, see {@link color3}.

color2.desc:
Color multiplier.

Values in this will be clamped to the 0-1 range. There is no equivalent property with unrestricted values based on the emission time of the particle, but {@link color3} is still multiplicative with this and can be used to scale the values indirectly.

color3.desc:
Color multiplier.

Values in this are unrestricted and can go above 1. If you want values to be clamped to the 0-1 range, see {@link color1}.

offsetUV.desc: Offset for the UV coordinates of the model.

speedUV.desc: Scroll speed for the model's texture.

offsetU.desc: Horizontal offset for the UV coordinates of the model.

offsetV.desc: Vertical offset for the UV coordinates of the model.

speedU.desc: Horiztonal scroll speed for the model's texture.

speedV.desc: Vertical scroll speed for the model's texture.

rgbMultiplier.desc: Scalar multiplier for the color that does not affect the alpha. Effectively a brightness multiplier.

orientation.desc: Rich model orientation mode. See {@link RichModelOrientationMode} for more information.

scaleVariationX.desc:
Each particle will pick a random number between this value and 1, and the width of the particle will be multiplied by this number. For example, setting this to 0.5 will make the particles randomly thinner, down to half width. Setting it to 2 will make them randomly wider, up to double width.

If {@link uniformScale} is enabled, this also affects the height.

scaleVariationY.desc:
Each particle will pick a random number between this value and 1, and the height of the particle will be multiplied by this number. For example, setting this to 0.5 will make the particles randomly shorter, down to half height. Setting it to 2 will make them randomly taller, up to double height.

If {@link uniformScale} is enabled, {@link scaleVariationX} also affects the height, and this field is ignored.

scaleVariationZ.desc:
Each particle will pick a random number between this value and 1, and the depth of the particle will be multiplied by this number. For example, setting this to 0.5 will make the particles randomly shallower, down to half depth. Setting it to 2 will make them randomly deeper, up to double depth. 

If {@link uniformScale} is enabled, {@link scaleVariationX} also affects the depth, and this field is ignored.

uniformScale.desc: If enabled, the particle X scale-related properties and fields will control the scale in all axes, and the Y and Z counterparts will be ignored.

dither.desc: If enabled, this allows control of the model's opacity regardless of its material by using dithered transparency. If disabled, changes to the alpha values that affect the particle will not have any effect unless the material allows it, but it will look better than the dithered transparency.

animation.desc: Controls which animation in the {@link anibnd} to play.

loopAnimation.desc: If disabled, the {@link animation} will only play once and then freeze on the last frame. If enabled, the animation will loop.

animationSpeed.desc: Controls the speed at which the {@link animation} plays.

unkBlendMode.desc:

This is somewhat similar to the `blendMode` property of other appearance actions, but the values do not match the ones in {@link BlendMode}.

bloomColor.desc:
Controls the color of the additional bloom effect. The colors of the particle will be multiplied with this color to get the final color of the bloom effect.

Note:

- This does not affect the natural bloom effect from high color values.

unk_ds3_f1_31.desc:
When this is set to 0, the wind will be able to affect sfx, including the one with this action. When it's set to 1, it seems to only affect non-sfx things, like plants and trees.

The way non-sfx are affected by the wind seems to also change a bit between values 0 and 1, but exactly how is unknown.

In DS3 and Sekiro, some effects have this set to 2, so it is not just a boolean. What 2 does is unknown.

forceRandomMultiplierMin.desc:
The minimum random multiplier for {@link force}. This multiplier will randomly change to different values in the range defined by this and {@link forceRandomMultiplierMax}.

This is multiplicative with both the base force and the {@link forceMultiplier other multiplier}.

forceRandomMultiplierMax.desc:
The maximum random multiplier for {@link force}. This multiplier will randomly change to different values in the range defined by this and {@link forceRandomMultiplierMin}.

This is multiplicative with both the base force and the {@link forceMultiplier other multiplier}.

forceMultiplier.desc:
A multiplier for {@link force}.

This is multiplicative with both the base force and the random multiplier.

fadeOutTime.desc: The time it takes for the force to fade out after the action has deactivated in seconds. Due to the way this value is stored, the time will be rounded to the nearest 1/30s.

actions.name: GravityForce

The name is from Elden Ring's RTTI, where it is named "GXForceFieldGravityAreaAppearance".

force.desc: The strength of the force applied in the volume.

shape.desc:
The shape of the volume.

Each shape has different fields controlling the size of the volume, and they also change where it scales from and what point things are being pulled towards:
| Shape | Fields | Origin | Center of mass |
|-|-|-|-|
| {@link ForceVolumeShape.Boundless Boundless} | *n/a* | *n/a* | Node position |
| {@link ForceVolumeShape.Sphere Sphere} | {@link sphereRadius} | Center of the sphere | Center of the sphere |
| {@link ForceVolumeShape.Box Box} | {@link boxSize} | Center of the box | Center of the box |

actions.desc:
Defines a chaotic force in a volume.

The name is from Elden Ring's RTTI, where it is named "GXForceFieldTurbulenceAreaAppearance".

noiseOffsetX.desc: Offset along the X-axis for the 3D noise used to control the strength and direction of the force in the volume.

noiseOffsetY.desc: Offset along the Y-axis for the 3D noise used to control the strength and direction of the force in the volume.

noiseOffsetZ.desc: Offset along the Z-axis for the 3D noise used to control the strength and direction of the force in the volume.

force.desc: The strength of the force applied in the volume.

shape.desc:
The shape of the volume.

Each shape has different fields controlling the size of the volume, and they also change where it scales from and what point things are being pulled towards:
| Shape | Fields | Origin |
|-|-|-|
| {@link ForceVolumeShape.Boundless Boundless} | *n/a* | *n/a* |
| {@link ForceVolumeShape.Sphere Sphere} | {@link sphereRadius} | Center of the sphere |
| {@link ForceVolumeShape.Box Box} | {@link boxSize} | Center of the box |
| {@link ForceVolumeShape.Cylinder Cylinder} | {@link cylinderHeight}, {@link cylinderRadius} | Slightly +Z of the center of the cylinder? |
| {@link ForceVolumeShape.SquarePrism SquarePrism} | {@link squarePrismHeight}, {@link squarePrismApothem} | Center of the base of the prism |

sphereRadius.desc: The radius of the {@link ForceVolumeShape.Sphere sphere} where the force is active.

boxSize.desc: The size of the {@link ForceVolumeShape.Box box} where the force is active.

cylinderHeight.desc: The height of the {@link ForceVolumeShape.Cylinder cylinder} where the force is active.

cylinderRadius.desc: The radius of the {@link ForceVolumeShape.Cylinder cylinder} where the force is active.

squarePrismHeight.desc: The height of the {@link ForceVolumeShape.SquarePrism square prism} where the force is active.

squarePrismApothem.desc: The apothem of the {@link ForceVolumeShape.SquarePrism square prism} where the force is active.

forceRandomMultiplierMin.desc: The minimum random multiplier for {@link force}. This multiplier will randomly change to different values in the range defined by this and {@link forceRandomMultiplierMax}.

forceRandomMultiplierMax.desc: The maximum random multiplier for {@link force}. This multiplier will randomly change to different values in the range defined by this and {@link forceRandomMultiplierMin}.

noiseScale.desc: The scale of the 3D noise used to control the strength and direction of the force in the volume. Lower values makes it more noisy, with small vortices forming everywhere. Higher values makes the noise smoother.

enableSoftRadius.desc: Controls whether or not {@link softRadius} is effective.

softRadius.desc:
The radius of a sphere where the force gets weaker with the distance from the origin. Very similar to the {@link sphereRadius sphere radius} when the {@link shape} of the volume is a sphere, but this has a smooth transition from inside the radius to the outside.

This requires {@link enableSoftRadius} to be enabled.

fadeOutTime.desc: The time it takes for the force to fade out after the action has deactivated in seconds. Due to the way this value is stored, the time will be rounded to the nearest 1/30s.

actions.name: Unk10400
actions.desc: Unknown root node action.

actions.name: Unk10500
actions.desc: Unknown root node action.

rateOfTime.desc: Controls how fast time passes for the entire effect.

limitViewDistance.desc: When enabled, this limits visibility of nodes outside of the distance defined by {@link maxViewDistance}.

maxViewDistance.desc: All nodes that are farther away from the camera than this will not be visible. This restriction requires {@link limitViewDistance} to be enabled.

initialSimulationTime.desc:
The game will simulate playing the effect for this amount of time in seconds before actually displaying the effect. This does not mean that it will delay displaying the effect, just that the effect will start as if it had already been playing for this time, kind of like skipping ahead in the animation. This doesn't affect everything in the effect, and a list of things affected has not been made, but it does affect periodic emitters at least.

Setting this to very high values can cause noticeable stutters in the game when the effect is spawned due to it having to simulate playing the effect for so long.

In Dark Souls 3, Sekiro, Elden Ring, and Nightreign, this value will be rounded to the nearest 1/30s due to how it is stored in the file format. It is stored differently in Armored Core 6, and so no rounding will happen for that.

actions.name: SpotLight
actions.desc: Defines a light source with an elliptic cone shape, a spot light.

diffuseColor.desc:
Controls the diffuse color of the light.

Values in this are unrestricted and can go above 1.

If {@link separateSpecular} is disabled, this also controls the specular color of the light.

specularColor.desc:
Controls the specular color of the light.

Values in this are unrestricted and can go above 1.

If {@link separateSpecular} is disabled, this property is ignored and {@link diffuseColor} controls both the diffuse as well as the specular color.

diffuseMultiplier.desc:
A scalar multiplier for the {@link diffuseColor diffuse color}. Good for easily adjusting the brightness of the light without changing the color.

If {@link separateSpecular} is disabled, this also affects the specular color of the light.

specularMultiplier.desc:
A scalar multiplier for the {@link specularColor specular color}.

If {@link separateSpecular} is disabled, this property is ignored.

near.desc: Controls where the light starts in the cone. It bascially "slices off" the tip of the cone. If set to 0, it acts as if it is set to 0.5.

far.desc: Controls how far away the base of the cone is from the light source.

radiusX.desc: The X radius for the elliptic base of the cone.

radiusY.desc: The Y radius for the elliptic base of the cone.

jitterAndFlicker.desc: Toggles the jitter and flicker animations for the light.

jitterAcceleration.desc: Controls the acceleration of the jittering.

jitterX.desc: Controls how much the light should move around randomly on the X-axis.

jitterY.desc: Controls how much the light should move around randomly on the Y-axis.

jitterZ.desc: Controls how much the light should move around randomly on the Z-axis.

flickerIntervalMin.desc: Controls the minimum interval for flickering.

flickerIntervalMax.desc: Controls the maximum interval for flickering.

flickerBrightness.desc: Brightness multiplier for the light when it flickers.

shadows.desc:
Controls if the light should have shadows or not.

Note: Map objects also have a setting for casting shadows, and both must be enabled for an object to cast shadows from the light source.

separateSpecular.desc: When enabled, this allows other properties and fields of the action to control the specular color independently of the diffuse color. When disabled, the diffuse counterpart of the properties or fields will affect both the diffuse and specular color.

shadowDarkness.desc: Controls how dark shadows from this light source are. At 0, the shadows will be entirely invisible.

fadeOutTime.desc:
The number of seconds the light takes to fade to nothing after being destroyed.

Due to how the field this represents works, the time will be rounded to the nearest multiple of 1/30s.

volumeDensity.desc: Controls the density of some sort of fake fog in the volume hit by the light. The fog does not affect the actual light produced by the source and is not affected by shadows.

phaseFunction.desc: Controls whether or not {@link asymmetryParam} affects the fake fog from {@link volumeDensity}.

asymmetryParam.desc:
Controls how the fake fog from {@link volumeDensity} scatters the light. This value is ignored if {@link phaseFunction} is disabled, and the fog will scatter the light equally in all directions.

- At 0, the light is scattered equally in every direction.
- As the value approaches 1, the light is scattered more and more forward, in the same direction as the light was already traveling. This means that the fake fog will be less visible from the side or behind, and more visible from in front of the light.
- At 1, the fog will not scatter the light at all, so it will be entirely invisible.
- Values above 1 produce unnatural-looking effects where the light darkens the fog instead.

adaptationExponent.desc: When not in a dark enough area, the brightness of the light will be multiplied by 0.1^α, where α is this exponent value. The light will have normal brightness when the area it's in is sufficiently dark.

ActionType.desc: Values used to represent different types of FXR actions.

None.desc: This action does nothing. It fits into most action slots and acts as a way to disable the effects of the other actions that go in those slots.

Unk10002_Fluid.desc: Unknown action that *may* exist in Dark Souls 3. It is not used in vanilla, but its name and ID have been found in the game's executable.

Unk10010_Tracer.desc: Unknown action that *may* exist in Dark Souls 3. It is not used in vanilla, but its name and ID have been found in the game's executable.

Unk20000_GPUBillboard.desc: Unknown action that exists in Elden Ring and possibly other games. It is not used in vanilla, but its name and ID have been found in the game's executable. Its structure is currently entirely unknown.

AttachMode.desc: Values used to represent different modes of attachment.

Parent.desc: Translates and rotates with the parent node.

DummyPoly.desc: Translates and rotates with the attachment point (dummypoly). Parent transformations are ignored.

ParentTranslation.desc: Only translates with the parent node. Rotations are entirely ignored.

DummyPolyTranslation.desc: Only translates with the attachment point (dummypoly). Rotations are entirely ignored.

BlendMode.desc: Values used to represent different types of blend modes.

Source.desc: Completely ignores blending. The source layer (particle) will be drawn in place of the background, ignoring the alpha of the layer.

Normal.desc:
The source layer (particle) will be drawn on over the background. Transparent or partially transparent parts of the layer will allow the background to be seen through the layer.

Also known as "source-over", and is the same as the "normal" blend mode found in many image editors.

Multiply.desc:
The source layer (particle) will be multiplied with the background, ignoring the alpha of the layer.

Same as the "multiply" blend mode found in many image editors.

Add.desc:
The source layer (particle) multiplied by its alpha (clamped to [0, 1]) will be added to the background.

Same as the "add", "additive", or "linear dodge" blend modes found in many image editors. The opposite of {@link Subtract}.

Subtract.desc:
The source layer (particle) multiplied by its alpha (clamped to [0, 1]) will be subtracted from the background.

Same as the "subtract" or "difference" blend modes found in many image editors. The opposite of {@link Add}.

ConfigType.desc: Values used to represent different types of node configurations, also known as "effects". There is one for each {@link NodeType type of node} that supports multiple configs.

LevelsOfDetail.desc:
Manages the duration and thresholds for the {@link NodeType.LevelsOfDetail levels of detail node}.

**Class**: {@link LevelsOfDetailConfig}

Basic.desc:
Config used in {@link NodeType.Basic basic nodes} to apply transforms and to control emission and properties of particles.

**Class**: {@link BasicConfig}

NodeEmitter.desc:
Config used in {@link NodeType.NodeEmitter node emitter nodes} to control the emission of child nodes.

**Class**: {@link NodeEmitterConfig}

DistortionMode.desc: Used by {@link ActionType.Distortion Distortion} particles to control what type of distortion to apply.

Stir.desc: Distorts the background as if you stuck something into it and stirred it. It is animated, and the stir speed is controlled by a property.

NormalMap.desc: Distorts the background based on the normal map.

Twist.desc: Distorts the background as if the edges were held in place and you grabbed the center and twisted it.

Unk4.desc: This seems to just squeeze everything to the bottom left corner?

DistortionShape.desc: Possible shapes for {@link ActionType.Distortion distortion} particles.

Hemiellipsoid.desc: Half of an ellipsoid. (Like a hemisphere, but with three different radii.)

Ellipsoid.desc: An ellipsoid. (Like a sphere, but with three different radii.)

Box.desc:
A cuboid.

The difference between this and {@link Box2} is how the
{@link GPUStandardParticle.emitterDistribution distribution} field acts on it.

Box2.desc:
A cuboid.

The difference between this and {@link Box} is how the
{@link GPUStandardParticle.emitterDistribution distribution} field acts on it.

Unk5.desc: Not yet tested. Found in 800020 in Sekiro.

ForceVolumeShape.desc: Values representing different shapes of the volume where force actions apply their force.

Boundless.desc: Allows the force to affect everything, everywhere.

Emitter.desc:
The direction will depend on the emitter shape.
| Emitter Shape | Direction |
|:-|:-|
| {@link ActionType.PointEmitterShape Point} | Same as {@link LocalNorth}. |
| {@link ActionType.DiskEmitterShape Disk} | Same as {@link LocalNorth}. |
| {@link ActionType.RectangleEmitterShape Rectangle} | Same as {@link LocalNorth}. |
| {@link ActionType.SphereEmitterShape Sphere} | The direction cannot be changed for this emitter shape. |
| {@link ActionType.BoxEmitterShape Box} | If {@link BoxEmitterShape.emitInside emitInside} is true, it picks a direction parallel to a random local axis. If it is false, the direction will be out from the box, perpendicular to the side where the particle was emitted. |
| {@link ActionType.CylinderEmitterShape Cylinder} | Out from the cylinder's axis. |

LightingMode.desc:
Values representing different lighting modes.

These values and the fields they are used in require more testing. It's best to not assume they will work exactly as described. Values not covered by this enum are also used in vanilla effects, so there are a lot of unknown things about this.

UnkMinus2.desc: Same as {@link Lit}, but this seems to sometimes have an extra light source from somewhere?

Unlit.desc: Lighting does not affect the particles. No shadows or specular hightlights.

Lit.desc: Lighting affects the particles just like most regular objects.

ModelOrientationMode.desc: Values representing different orientation modes for {@link ActionType.Model Model} particles.

CameraPlane.desc: Faces away from the camera plane, the same direction as the camera itself.

ParticleDirection.desc: Faces in the direction the particle is moving. This direction can be modified by {@link ActionSlots.DirectionSpreadAction DirectionSpread actions}, and is initially the particle's {@link InitialDirection}.

GlobalPitch.desc:
Tries to face the camera, but is limited to rotation around the global X-axis.

Seemingly identical to {@link UnkGlobalPitch}?

GlobalYaw.desc: Tries to face the camera, but is limited to rotation around the vertical global Y-axis.

UnkGlobalPitch.desc:
Tries to face the camera, but is limited to rotation around the global X-axis.

Seemingly identical to {@link GlobalPitch}?

NodeType.desc: Values used to represent different types of FXR nodes.

Root.desc:
The root of the FXR tree structure.

**Class**: {@link RootNode}

Proxy.desc:
Acts as a node containing another SFX.

**Class**: {@link ProxyNode}

LevelsOfDetail.desc:
A node that only displays one of its child nodes at a time based on distance thresholds for each.

**Class**: {@link LevelsOfDetailNode}

Basic.desc:
A basic node that can emit particles, play sounds, have transforms and child nodes.

**Class**: {@link BasicNode}

NodeEmitter.desc:
A node that emits its child nodes.

**Class**: {@link NodeEmitterNode}

OrientationMode.desc: Values representing different orientation modes for most particles.

LocalSouth.desc: Faces the -Z direction of the parent node.

UnkSouth.desc:
Faces global south.

Similar to {@link South}, but this seems to change the projection of the particle in some way.

GlobalYaw.desc: Tries to face the camera, but is limited to rotation around the vertical global Y-axis.

Camera.desc:
Faces the camera.

This is different from {@link CameraPlane}, as this makes it face the camera's position instead of the camera plane.

LocalYaw.desc: Tries to face the camera, but is limited to rotation around the Y-axis of the parent node.

Unk11.desc: Not yet tested. Found in 639742 in Elden Ring. This also implies the existence of 8, 9, and 10, but they have not been tested or found yet.

PropertyArgument.desc:
Arguments used when evaluating properties.

There is no way to change what argument is given to a property. Each property has one specific argument given to it, and this is sometimes the only difference between two properties in the same action.

ParticleAge.desc: Time in seconds since the particle was emitted.

ActiveTime.desc:
Time in seconds since the action became active.

An action becoming active is for example the delay from {@link ActionType.NodeAttributes NodeAttributes} being over, or the active {@link State} changing, making a node change which of its configs is active.

EmissionTime.desc: Time in seconds between the effect being created and the particle being emitted. Stays constant per particle.

ExternalValue.desc:
An external value.

In property modifiers, which external value is used is controlled by a field in the modifier.

ReflectionMode.desc: Used by {@link ActionType.LensFlare lens flares} to control the direction of the offset vector.

None.desc: No offsets. The flare(s) will appear at the source's position.

Radial.desc: The source's screen-space position will be reflected through the center of the screen to calculate the offset vector.

Horizontal.desc: The source's screen-space position will be flipped horizontally to calculate the offset vector.

RichModelOrientationMode.desc: Values representing different orientation modes for {@link ActionType.RichModel RichModel} particles.

North.desc:
Faces global north.

Seemingly identical to {@link UnkNorth}?

CameraPlane.desc: Faces away from the camera plane, the same direction as the camera itself.

ParticleDirection.desc: Faces in the direction the particle is moving. This direction can be modified by {@link ActionSlots.DirectionSpreadAction DirectionSpread actions}, and is initially the particle's {@link InitialDirection}.

UnkNorth.desc:
Faces global north.

Seemingly identical to {@link North}?

GlobalYaw.desc: Tries to face the camera, but is limited to rotation around the vertical global Y-axis.

TracerOrientationMode.desc: Values representing different orientation modes for {@link ActionType.Tracer Tracer} and {@link ActionType.LegacyTracer LegacyTracer} particles.

Travel.desc: The tracer source is perpendicular to the direction it's travelling and the direction of the camera.

LocalZ.desc: The tracer source is aligned with the local Z-axis, which is detenmined by the rotation of the node that emits the tracer.

Vertical.desc: The tracer source is aligned with the global vertical axis.

GlobalX.desc: The tracer source is aligned with the global X-axis.

Cross.desc: Creates two sources for the tracer with different orientation modes. One has {@link Vertical} and the other has {@link GlobalX}, forming a cross.

Diagonal.desc: The tracer source is parallel to the global diagonal (1, 1, 1).
